name: Secure Network / VPN
description: Manages and reports secure-network (VPN) connection state through provider control-plane APIs, with a pluggable provider architecture.
author: OrchPilot

nodes.description: Connect, disconnect, check, test and wait on a VPN connection across AWS, Azure, GCP and generic IPsec / OpenVPN / WireGuard. Reports real provider state; a control-plane plugin that does not fake connectivity or dial tunnels.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Which VPN this node acts on. Provider-specific fields appear below.

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: For cloud providers CONNECT reports the tunnel state — there is no dial operation. TEST_CONNECTION states exactly what it checked.

connectionProfile.title: Connection profile / credential id
connectionProfile.description: Names a stored credential whose parts are the secrets <profile>.<name>, e.g. aws-prod.accessKeyId and aws-prod.secretKey. Select a profile instead of entering credentials on every node.

connectionId.title: Connection id
connectionId.description: The provider connection identifier — an AWS vpn-…, an Azure connection name, a GCP tunnel. Supports variables such as ${vpn.connectionId}.

endpointHost.title: Endpoint host override
endpointHost.description: Rarely needed. Overrides the provider's default API host (a GovCloud or sovereign endpoint). Must be on the plugin's allowed hosts.

protocol.title: Protocol
protocol.description: OpenVPN only. TCP lets this node open a real reachability socket to the port.

timeoutSeconds.title: Timeout (seconds)
timeoutSeconds.description: For a wait. On expiry the node fails with VPN_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT.

credentials.description: Credentials come from the secret store and only from there — there is no field on the node that holds a key. A connection profile names a stored credential whose parts are the secrets <profile>.<name>. AWS: accessKeyId, secretKey, optional sessionToken. Azure/GCP: accessToken (an OAuth bearer token the environment already mints). IPsec: presharedKey (or certificate/privateKey). OpenVPN: caCertificate, clientCertificate, clientKey, username, password. WireGuard: privateKey, optional presharedKey.

permissions.notes: Cloud providers call their control-plane APIs through the engine's HTTP client, so they are bound by this plugin's allowed hosts — grant the specific host you use (e.g. ec2.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com) with Plugins → the version → Edit. The 'network' list here is a suggestion, not a grant. The generic providers (IPsec/OpenVPN/WireGuard) open a TCP reachability socket to the configured endpoint for OpenVPN-over-TCP only; that socket is not bound by the allowed-hosts guard, which covers the HTTP client. This plugin does not bring tunnels up and never runs a privileged VPN client.
